name: IVAM Institut Valencià d'Art Modern
funding: Run by the Generalitat Valenciana's culture department; no operating budget found. 202,258 visitors in 2025. It bought 16 works by 14 women artists for about EUR 1M.
watch: Director Enguita resigned in February 2024 after the Vox-led culture department, which funds IVAM, reported her land donation to prosecutors. They archived it in March.
why_flagged: Run by the Generalitat Valenciana's culture department; no operating budget found. 202,258 visitors in 2025. It bought 16 works by 14 women artists for about EUR 1M.
records_note: No annual report; accounts for 2012 to 2025 with audit reports are posted, the Consejo Rector is listed, and sponsors appear only as two logos.

name: Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation
funding: Private foundation endowed by oilman Calouste Gulbenkian's fortune; assets EUR 4.0bn at end 2025. It owned oil firm Partex until selling it to PTTEP in November 2019.
watch: Partex was about 18% of its investments. Ten protesters entered a Foundation conference in March 2016 and cited its ownership of Partex.
why_flagged: Private foundation endowed by oilman Calouste Gulbenkian's fortune; assets EUR 4.0bn at end 2025. It owned oil firm Partex until selling it to PTTEP in November 2019.
records_note: Annual reports with certified accounts run from 2012 to 2025 and the board is listed; it publishes no donor list.

name: MAC/CCB Museu de Arte Contemporânea do Centro Cultural de Belém
funding: Run by Fundação CCB, whose bodies the Culture and Finance ministers appoint. The State Budget gives about EUR 10.5M; the 2025 subsidy was unchanged. MAC/CCB had 588,643 visitors in 2024.
watch: The Culture Minister removed CCB president Francisca Carneiro Fernandes in November 2024. A petition drew 2,000+ signatures; in 2026 the State admitted no grounds.
why_flagged: Run by Fundação CCB, whose bodies the Culture and Finance ministers appoint. The State Budget gives about EUR 10.5M; the 2025 subsidy was unchanged. MAC/CCB had 588,643 visitors in 2024.
records_note: Reports run 2021 to 2025, with audited accounts in the 2024 one; a 2023 to 2025 table of support names funders; the board is listed.

name: Onassis Stegi
funding: Run by the Alexander S. Onassis Foundation, funded entirely by profits of its Business Foundation, which invests in shipping and real estate. Corporate sponsors exist; no budget is published.
watch: Onassis built his fortune on tankers chartered to oil majors: no flag. Teachers stopped work in February 2025 against the Foundation's Onassis Public Schools.
why_flagged: Onassis built his fortune on tankers chartered to oil majors: no flag. Teachers stopped work in February 2025 against the Foundation's Onassis Public Schools.
records_note: The Onassis Foundation site is behind a bot check, so its reports, accounts, sponsor page and board could not be checked.

name: DESTE Foundation for Contemporary Art
funding: Private foundation set up in Geneva in 1983 by collector Dakis Joannou, a construction and hotel businessman.
watch: Runs the Athens space and the Slaughterhouse Project Space on Hydra, granted by the island's municipality in 2008. NEON belongs to Daskalopoulos, not Joannou.
records_note: DESTE's About page names no donors or sponsors, and the site publishes no annual reports, accounts or board.

name: Nicosia Municipal Arts Centre (NiMAC)
funding: Nicosia Municipality and the Pierides Foundation run it under a cooperation agreement. Shows credit the Deputy Ministry of Culture, A.G. Leventis Foundation and European University Cyprus. No budget is published.
watch: A 2026 show with Emin Cizenel, who designed the north's flag, drew a small protest and a deputy mayor's call to cancel. No cancellation reported.
why_flagged: Nicosia Municipality and the Pierides Foundation run it under a cooperation agreement. Shows credit the Deputy Ministry of Culture, A.G. Leventis Foundation and European University Cyprus. No budget is published.
records_note: One annual report covers 2024 and 2025; no accounts, funder list or board appear, though exhibition pages credit funders.

name: MICAS Malta International Contemporary Art Space
funding: A EUR 30M project funded by the Maltese state and the European Regional Development Fund; the gallery works were co-financed 80% EU, 20% national.
watch: A EUR 0.5M Rondinone sculpture was bought with no public call via board member Francis Sultana, who sells Rondinone. The minister denies a conflict.
why_flagged: A EUR 0.5M Rondinone sculpture was bought with no public call via board member Francis Sultana, who sells Rondinone. The minister denies a conflict.
records_note: Names four board members and an international committee on its about page; publishes no annual report, accounts or sponsor list.

name: Sónar Festival
funding: Owned by Superstruct Entertainment, which KKR acquired in 2024. Its site shows the Generalitat, Estrella Damm and drinks brands. Sónar says it sends KKR no money. No budget found.
watch: In June 2025 at least 34 acts, including Arca and Rone, withdrew over KKR's Israel investments and its stake in Sónar's owner.
why_flagged: Owned by Superstruct Entertainment, which KKR acquired in 2024. Its site shows the Generalitat, Estrella Damm and drinks brands. Sónar says it sends KKR no money. No budget found.
records_note: It posts no reports, accounts or board; the site footer shows partner logos, undated, including Estrella Damm, Fritz-kola, the Generalitat and Barcelona City Council.

name: National Gallery - Alexandros Soutzos Museum
funding: Greek state museum. The ministry assured EUR 42M of the EUR 59M expansion (2021). The Stavros Niarchos Foundation gave EUR 13M in 2017.
watch: March 2025: MP Nikos Papadopoulos damaged four works he called blasphemous. September: 400 believers sought a court ban on the show; refused.
why_flagged: Greek state museum. The ministry assured EUR 42M of the EUR 59M expansion (2021). The Stavros Niarchos Foundation gave EUR 13M in 2017.
records_note: It posts no annual reports, accounts or sponsor list; its structure page names the board of directors, and its footer links to the Diavgeia register.

name: Kampala Art Biennale
funding: Produced by Kampala Arts Trust and Afriart Gallery. KAB20 (2020) was co-funded by the EU and Pro Helvetia. TotalEnergies Foundation backed the 2018 mentoring programme; no later TotalEnergies money found.
watch: Founded in 2014 by Daudi Karungi. No edition since the virtual KAB20 in 2020; the site is now an archive.
records_note: Publishes no annual reports or accounts; its Partners page names the KAB20 co-funders, and the producing Kampala Arts Trust names its seven trustees.

name: Addis Foto Fest
funding: Produced by Desta for Africa, directed by Aida Muluneh. The last sponsor list is from 2018: Swiss Embassy, Canon, National Geographic Society, Marriott and others. None published since.
watch: Founded 2010. The fifth edition opened 6 December 2018. A sixth was announced for December 2020; no edition since is documented.
records_note: addisfotofest.com lists no sponsors, reports, accounts or board; it posts festival catalogues for 2010 to 2018 and names Desta for Africa as producer.

name: Rwanda Art Museum
funding: Owned and run by the Rwanda Cultural Heritage Academy, the government body that runs Rwanda's national museums.
watch: Opened in 2009 in the former presidential palace at Kanombe and renamed the Rwanda Art Museum in 2018.
records_note: Publishes nothing itself: its parent, the Rwanda Cultural Heritage Academy, posts laws and policies but no annual reports, accounts, funders or board.
